answers.answer: Select number of players + 1 Factory cards face-down, return the rest to the box without looking. Place one encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly choose a structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts; play proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup: Factory cards, encounter tokens, structure bonus; lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.

answers.answer: The character starts at home base; two workers start on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining home base; four mechs sit over their Faction Mat abilities; six stars by the faction emblem; six technology cubes in the marked green Player Mat boxes; four structures in their matching boxes; four recruits in bottom-row circular spaces; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; action token beside the Player Mat. Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins, and two objectives.
answers.evidence: Setup piece table and steps 3–4.

answers.answer: You may take neither action after moving the token, but must move it to a different section. Rusviet may repeat a section including Factory; top and bottom actions still each occur at most once that turn. You cannot take bottom before top when taking both. Top-row gains may pay bottom-row costs. Pay the full exposed red-box cost first; then take as much or as little exposed green-box benefit as desired. Costs and benefits vary by mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: different section, optional actions, full cost then optional benefit.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls the territory and all its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you keep those abilities except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. You may spend resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: enemy worker alone; abilities; resources from any controlled territories.

answers.answer: On the normal Move, select up to two different units and move each one adjacent territory; one unit cannot use both selections to move twice. Mechs can carry any number of your workers (but never your character); all units can carry any number of resources. A carried worker may subsequently move itself, or may board a mech and be carried by its subsequent move.
answers.evidence: Top-row Move OR coins: two different units; carrying rules.

answers.answer: The mech may enter enemy-workers-only territory, then stops and cannot move again that turn; the enemy workers immediately retreat to their home base leaving resources. You lose one popularity per worker, down to zero, and insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat. Your workers cannot independently enter that territory while enemy workers control it.
answers.evidence: Top-row Move: Enemy workers only; Speed stops overridden.

answers.answer: After all units finish the Move action, resolve combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. Workers cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Top-row Move: Enemy character/mechs; Combat opening.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card; if the draw deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck, and if both are empty draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity. Traded resources go on a controlled territory containing at least one worker; if all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.
answers.evidence: Bolster; Trade.

answers.answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost in full before producing. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that same territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and are placed in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Newly exposed costs affect future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce steps 1–3.

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat; it moves a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost. Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes; place a chosen mech on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake; its ability then applies to your character and every mech, not workers. Even when all upgrades/mechs/structures/recruits are complete, you may still pay for the bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade; Deploy; completed bottom actions.

answers.answer: Build on a controlled territory containing your worker; only one structure total may be on a territory, including opponents' structures, and lakes/home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. The Mill adds a bonus Produce territory only while you control it; if enemies occupy its territory and you lack control, it cannot produce. Your Mine is a personal tunnel for your unit movement to and from it even while enemy units occupy its territory, subject to ordinary entry/combat restrictions; opponents cannot use its ability.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row Build; Control; Mine movement.

answers.answer: Put the recruit permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat; immediately gain two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards, according to the chosen space. Its ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed from the Player Mat. For ongoing bonuses, resolve active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor; stop if a sixth star ends play. In two-player play, the opponent triggers it once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist; Ongoing recruits.

answers.answer: Both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose dial power from 0 to the smaller of seven and their current power, then may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech (Rusviet People's Army adds one total if workers are present). If both have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously, add dial and card values, and attacker wins ties. Both pay their selected dial power from the Power Track; played cards are discarded face-up and their values do not cost extra track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–4.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory/resources. Losing characters, mechs, and workers all retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy may instead send eligible units/carried workers to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, even workers carried by defeated mechs on lakes; a winning defender loses none, subject to Polania Camaraderie. A non-Saxony winner earns a combat star if they have zero or one combat stars, and none if already at two; Saxony places one after every victory while star tokens remain. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on dial or through cards; a zero-total loser gets none.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 5–6.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains on the encounter territory, discard the token and draw/resolve an encounter before a following bottom action. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. Gains of resources, workers, mechs, and structures go to the encounter territory. Pay the printed encounter cost, but no additional normal action costs apply and no additional mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses are gained.
answers.evidence: Encounters: timing, contested entry, placement and costs.

answers.answer: Every player's character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if needed), looks at available Factory cards, chooses one, and returns the rest. This is not limited to the first visitor. Each player gets at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. The card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom subject to usual no-repeat rules (Rusviet exception), and Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories within that Move action, or three for a Speed-enabled character/mech; normal restrictions apply.
answers.evidence: Factory.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective; you may wait, but must satisfy all requirements at reveal. Place a star on the Triumph Track objective space and return the completed card to the bottom of the objective deck. Normally return your other objective card too. Saxony may complete both starting objectives, keeps the other after the first, and can earn up to two objective stars.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power; each goal is awarded once except combat's two stars and Saxony's exception. A placed star is permanent even if power/popularity later drops, and another player's star never blocks a goal. The sixth star immediately ends play with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end.

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, collect its primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing that star. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement and return initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat. For neighbor recruit bonuses, finish the active action, then resolve active player first, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for a sixth star each time; if an earlier player places the sixth star, later recruit stars/bonuses do not resolve.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end: bottom-row action sequence, neighbor bonuses and unresolved battle.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, the 7–12 tier pays $4 per star, $3 per territory count, and $2 per complete resource pair. Five stars add $20; four normal territories plus the Factory count as 7, adding $21; 13 resources make 6 pairs, adding $12. These categories add $53 to held coins, before any structure bonus. Your structures qualify for the selected structure bonus even if enemies control their territories. Tiebreakers: workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune: popularity table, territory scoring, structure eligibility; tie order.

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move back into any home base, build there, or deploy there; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea's unlocked Wayfare. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases.

answers.answer: Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, and villages workers; lakes and the Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Produce terrain table; Control/resources: only four resource types and no token supply limit.

answers.answer: All units may pick up, carry, and drop off any number of resources during movement; only mechs may also carry any number of your workers, never your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump still costs one movement step and the extra step may be before or after it; a mech can pick up/drop resources and workers mid-movement. Enemy-unit and character-encounter stops override Speed.
answers.evidence: Top-row Move: carrying and Speed.

answers.answer: Yes. Any unit may enter a territory occupied only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Top-row Move: Enemy structure only; printed tunnel territories.

answers.answer: You may not pay only part of a cost. If unable to afford any action after using Move last turn, make a dead turn: move the token to a different section and take neither action.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: dead turn; never pay only part of a cost.

answers.answer: A built Armory grants one power on Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity on Bolster. These apply when you take the corresponding top action. You keep structure abilities even without control, though an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce; enemies do not gain your structure's abilities.
answers.evidence: Bolster; Trade; Control; Build structure abilities.

answers.answer: Riverwalk is an unlockable mech ability for every faction, including Nordic, and lets the character and all mechs cross rivers to faction-specific destinations: Nordic/Saxony forests and mountains; Rusviet farms and villages; Crimea farms and tundra; Polania villages and mountains. It does not apply to workers. Nordic's starting Swim lets workers cross rivers to any land terrain but not lakes; it does not give Nordic mechs lake movement. Nordic mechs/character get lake movement only from unlocked Seaworthy.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities: Riverwalk table; Nordic Swim and Seaworthy.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels, including your Mine, adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Workers cannot use these shortcuts.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Saxony Underpass; Rusviet Township.

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine; once per combat (not per unit), the opponent loses two power on the track. Nordic Artillery instead may be used before combat by paying one power to reduce the opponent's power by two; it too is once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Saxony Disarm; Nordic Artillery.

answers.answer: Two mechs and three workers may play three cards total in combat with Rusviet People's Army: one per participating character/mech plus one additional card total when at least one worker is present. Workers alone never fight.
answers.evidence: Rusviet People's Army; Combat cards.

answers.answer: With unlocked Wayfare, Crimea's character/mechs may move from a territory or home base to its own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. They cannot enter an active opponent's home base.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare.

answers.answer: Scout lets Crimea steal one random combat card from the opponent into its hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion lets Crimea spend one combat card as any one resource regardless of card value, once per turn.
answers.evidence: Crimea Scout; starting special ability Coercion.

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to and from lakes and lets them retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home. Polania Submerge also allows character/mechs to move from any lake to any other lake, but Polania has no adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, workers on lakes require a mech to move off; you cannot leave carried workers or resources behind on a lake when their carrier leaves.
answers.evidence: Nordic Seaworthy; Polania Submerge and lake rules.

answers.answer: Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins combat as aggressor on its turn. It does not prevent popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Polania Camaraderie.

answers.answer: Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order. The first gain may pay the second option's cost; pay the printed cost and take as much or as little benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Polania Meander; Encounters options and costs.

answers.answer: No. A character entering an encounter-token territory, including during Factory Move, stops and cannot move again that turn. Resolve the encounter after the whole Move action and all combats, only if the character remains there.
answers.evidence: Top-row Move encounter rule; Encounters; Factory.

answers.answer: Coins are not hidden information, but you need not reveal their total value when asked. Combat-card hand count is public; in combat you may conceal whether you committed any combat cards until reveal, and card contents are secret until revealed. Objective contents are secret until you reveal a completed objective.
answers.evidence: Public and hidden information table.

answers.answer: Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable in informal agreements; agreements are unenforceable. In tournament play even coin exchanges for deals/alliances are forbidden. A payment cannot cancel combat already initiated by moving units onto opposing units; fight after Move, though bribes may influence the outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements.

answers.answer: Popularity 0–6: $3 per star, $2 per territory count, $1 per complete pair of controlled resources. Popularity 7–12: $4, $3, and $2 respectively. Popularity 13–18: $5, $4, and $3 respectively. Controlled lakes count; home bases do not. Pool resources across controlled territories and ignore an odd leftover token.
answers.evidence: Final fortune popularity table and scoring rules.

answers.answer: For each adjacency tile, count unique qualifying printed features across all your structures, so duplicates count once. Rivers do not break adjacency. Adjacent tunnel territories are unique printed tunnels, not Mines: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6=$9. Adjacent encounter locations are unique printed locations even if their token was removed: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6–7=$9. Adjacent lakes are unique lakes: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6–7=$9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility: adjacency tiles.

answers.answer: Structures on tunnels count structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3–4=$6. Structures in a row score only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break the line: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9. Structures on farms/tundras count qualifying structures combined: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility: structures on tunnels, in a row, and on farms/tundras.

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.
answers.evidence: Combat step 6.

answers.answer: No. A placed popularity star is permanent, but current popularity determines final scoring, so it does not protect current popularity or preserve its scoring tier. Other players' stars never block a goal, so two factions can each star the same achievement.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end; Final fortune.

answers.answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Sit near your faction's home base; clockwise seating order from the board top is Nordic → Rusviet → Crimea → Saxony → Polania, omitting inactive factions. Seating identifies immediate left/right neighbors who may receive ongoing recruit bonuses when the active player takes a matching bottom action.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2 and Ongoing recruits.

answers.answer: A river is a border between two land territories. A lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with an applicable lake-movement ability may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
answers.evidence: Top-row Move: river and lake movement.

answers.answer: No, you may not keep the drawn encounter card private. Show it to all players, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud; you need not read every option aloud.
answers.evidence: Encounters: show card and read text.

answers.answer: No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: no limit.

answers.answer: After the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, the next clockwise player may begin their turn while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure, or recruit to gain.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: next clockwise player may begin.

answers.answer: No. Taking a top action and bottom action is limited to once each within the turn, including for Rusviet. The token must move to a different section from last turn; Rusviet's repeat ability waives only that previous-turn section restriction.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: repeat section and action limits.

answers.answer: You may instead gain $1 from the normal unupgraded Move action.
answers.evidence: Top-row Move OR coins.

answers.answer: No. Workers never return to the Player Mat; a worker forced to retreat goes to its home base, and Produce takes new workers from the Player Mat left to right.
answers.evidence: Produce: workers never return; enemy workers retreat to home base.

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power and zero popularity, including both at zero.
answers.evidence: Combat opening.

answers.answer: Yes. You may still fight after reaching the two combat-star limit; the non-Saxony winner then places no further combat star.
answers.evidence: Combat step 5.

answers.answer: A faction without Meander must choose one affordable option and cannot decline to choose any option. It cannot select an unaffordable coin/popularity option. After choosing, it may take as little of that option's benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Encounters: factions without Meander and benefits.

answers.answer: No. Combatants choose dial power simultaneously and secretly, not in turn order. They reveal simultaneously after choosing dial and optional cards.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3.

answers.answer: Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: announce action.

answers.answer: No. Place a star as soon as you achieve a star goal; stars are permanent and the sixth immediately ends the game. A completed objective is different: you may wait to reveal it, but must meet all requirements at the moment you reveal it on your own turn.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end; Objectives and agreements.

answers.answer: Normally, units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes. Faction and mech abilities provide exceptions.
answers.evidence: Top-row Move: river/lake restrictions.

answers.answer: No. The recruit is put permanently on the chosen open one-time bonus space and cannot later move.
answers.evidence: Enlist: recruit cannot later move.

answers.answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter; a character entering the token territory stops and cannot move again that turn.
answers.evidence: Encounters; Top-row Move encounter rule.

answers.answer: While controlled, the Mill adds one bonus production territory to your current Produce allowance: two normal territories become up to three, or an upgraded allowance of three becomes up to four. The Mill itself counts as one producing worker; each actual worker there also produces normally, so Mill output is added to their output. The Mill can produce with no actual worker there, using the terrain table.
answers.evidence: Produce: Mill paragraph.

answers.answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish or preserve control; if your last unit leaves and you have no qualifying structure, you do not control it.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: control definition; only resources are resources.

answers.answer: Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row resources: Upgrade oil; Deploy metal; Build wood; Enlist food.
